content: Expect a solid reporting season but share prices to be largely driven by factors other than fundamentals

Going into Q2 reporting season, our checks and industry conversations point to a mixed picture with some companies such as SAP likely to see a fairly stable demand environment (despite the challenging geopolitical backdrop) while the picture is very diverse across Engineering Software and IT Services. In Engineering Software, we prefer higher-quality names with stronger recurring revenue profiles and lower cyclical exposure, while in IT Services outcomes are likely to diverge more meaningfully, with limited Middle East exposure leaving players such as Capgemini better shielded from recent geopolitical disruption despite ongoing weakness in discretionary spending. While headline risk from new AI model launches seems to have somewhat subsided (i.e. Software stocks react less) due to already very bearish investor positioning across hedge funds but also long onlies, we do not expect Q2 to be a turning point yet even for names with decent/better-than-feared quarters. The main driver of Software share prices remains positioning and the relative strength of AI Semis/Hardware, in our view, combined with medium-term uncertainty around the financial model for SITS players in an AI world. The latter is likely to change as we go into 2027 where we expect major players such as SAP and Dassault to provide more of a framework around how to model its AI business and financial opportunity towards the end of this decade (and beyond). Yet, for now it remains wait and see with new customer wins and AI contract proof points being what the market should focus on, in our view, in order to gauge success of the AI strategies of the companies within our coverage.
All eyes on more AI proof points from SAP

Following new AI solutions announcements at Sapphire 2026, we see additional customer proof points and details on commercial success as key from here (and more important than results). Our checks indicate good customer feedback on the new AI offering post Sapphire with the availability of large parts of SAP's AI roadmap to on-prem customers (if they sign a RISE Cloud migration deal) a catalyst for many Cloud migration latecomers to make the move. This should help Cloud growth towards next year and FY28, in our view. SAP will have to provide some incremental KPIs and a more detailed financial framework around the AI opportunity, which is expected to account for ~1/3 of Cloud revenues by 2030, at one point. We would expect this with Q4 results or Sapphire 2027 after the company has been able to sign AI deals based on their new offering for 6-12 months.

Key takes on Q2 by subsector

Within large-cap Software, we expect a solid Q2 for SAP. We see current Cloud backlog (CCB) growth for Q2 at ~25%, in-line with company guidance for slightly decelerating CCB growth throughout FY26 and slightly towards the upper end of where we see market expectations (24-25% incl. M&A). Healthy bookings momentum should drive continued close to 30% growth for its Cloud ERP Suite, from ~30% y/y cc in Q1/26, accounting for headwinds from only slightly growing transactional revenues. We model Q2/26 Cloud revenue growth at ~23% y/y cc and overall P&L metrics to be broadly in-line while consensus FCF for Q2 appears too high (distorted by outliers). Most importantly, we expect SAP to reiterate its FY26 cc outlook for revenues, EBIT and FCF which should remove fears over a potential guidance cut related to the Middle East situation. Having said that, investment in product/AI as well as infrastructure rollouts (mostly for sovereign Cloud) could limit margin upside into H2 and next year as management alluded to at Sapphire in May already. For Sage, we believe the momentum will continue in FQ3/26 but tougher comps could be a slight offset. With strong momentum in ARR, we believe Sage will easily achieve its full year target of >9% top-line growth. We are modelling recurring revenue growth of 9.7% organically on continued momentum for Intacct especially outside the US and helped by Copilot monetization and well supported by Sage Business Cloud (H1/26 growth of 15% y/y) including Cloud native revenue growth (H1/26: 25% y/y). For Amadeus, Q2 is likely to mark the trough in volumes, with bookings and passengers boarded remaining under pressure following the Middle East disruption. However, resilient unit revenues, pricing and mix should help cushion the impact. The key focus is likely to be on guidance, where the recent escalation in the region has reduced our confidence in the company's ability to deliver within the lower end of its current outlook. While activity improved through June, we believe the balance of risk remains skewed towards a more cautious stance on FY26 expectations and therefore maintain our Hold recommendation.

We value the sector on a mix of P/E, EV/uFCF, EV/EBIT(DA), DCF and SOTP valuations, benchmarking multiples vs. peers' and/or expected growth rates. Key sector risks include macro, FX, regulation, new technologies, potentially value-destructive M&A and market-share shifts.

We remain selective in Engineering Software. Near-term macro risk is rising, and we do not think guidances fully capture the potential second-order effects from the prolonged Iran conflict on customer decision-making and deal timelines, which will likely only become visible throughout the year. Direct exposure to the Middle East is limited across players in our coverage, but given the broader uncertainty, we prefer higher-quality names with a higher share of recurring revenue and less exposure to potentially affected, cyclical end-markets. At the same time, AI-native challengers making inroads and targeting specific use-cases across the engineering stack remain a headline risk, with new partnership announcements likely to keep pressure on sentiment. Within Buy-rated names, we expect a guidance update from Nemetschek to incorporate the recently closed HCSS acquisition, confirming 14-15% cc organic growth and add a high-single-digit contribution from HCSS. On margins, we expect Nemetschek to confirm the 32-33% underlying EBITDA margin but see M&A related one-off costs to weight on the reported number. Q2 itself should be decent for Nemetschek, driven by still strong growth in Build segment and decent growth in Design despite tough comps, while we remain cautious on Media. IT Services continues to face a muted demand backdrop, with discretionary spending yet to recover meaningfully and recent geopolitical tensions adding further uncertainty to customer decision-making and deal timing. At the same time, sentiment remains weighed down by ongoing questions around how AI will reshape delivery models, pricing and the competitive landscape as hyperscalers and model providers continue to build out their deployment capabilities. Capgemini remains our preferred name within IT Services. Limited exposure to the Middle East should help insulate the company from recent geopolitical disruption, and we believe Q2 could prove particularly strong relative to peers. With our forecasts already ahead of the current guidance framework, supported by strong momentum in the UK and US as well as ongoing strength in BPO, we do not rule out a guidance raise this quarter. Reply remains one of our preferred names in the sector. Q1 reassured on both growth and margins, and we continue to see scope for improvement through the year, supported by ongoing strength in Italy and the US, improving trends in Germany and a continued recovery in France. We also expect investors to focus on the early traction of the recently launched Reply Model Factory and whether this translates into incremental demand opportunities. Within resellers, we continue to prefer Bechtle over Cancom and SoftwareOne. Following the recent guidance increase and constructive CMD, however, we also expect another solid quarter from SoftwareOne. Having benefited from several large renewals in Q1, Q2 should provide a cleaner test of underlying demand and the operational trajectory of the combined SoftwareOne-Crayon platform. Focus is likely to center on North America, channel trends, margins and free cash flow execution.

Within SMID-cap names in our coverage, we expect sequential improvement in Q2 for ATOSS Software, albeit somewhat helped by more favorable comps, while the EBIT margin should be broadly flat sequentially. That said, with the stock stuck in the "disadvantaged by AI" basket, we expect the focus to be on KPIs to assess any potential AI impact (NRR, GRR, ARR growth,...). For Mensch und Maschine, we expect Q2 growth to remain below the mid-term target range, despite Digitization still benefiting from lower comps as H1/25 was impacted by headwinds related to the change in the Autodesk partner model, with a lower share of multi-year renewals in the Autodesk reselling business weighing on growth. Still, we expect the Software segment to remain robust in Q2 but not enough to make a difference on group level. AutoStore should deliver another strong quarter, supported by healthy activity levels across key end-markets and continued strength in North America. While favorable comparables remain supportive, investor focus is likely to center on whether the recent Middle East disruption had any meaningful impact on momentum through Q2. For Netcompany, we expect another solid quarter, supported by continued UK momentum. Amadeus (Hold) - weaker volumes, resilient pricing, focus on guidance We expect Amadeus to report Q2 revenue growth of 3.1% cc y/y to E1,665m vs cons at E1,656m, reflecting a materially weaker travel backdrop, particularly in Air Distribution, partly offset by resilient unit revenues and continued cost control. The key issue for the quarter is not only the Q2 volume weakness, but whether trends in June and early July are sufficient to support the FY outlook.

External traffic data point to a clear deterioration through Q2. IATA reported global RPK growth of -3.4% y/y in April and -2.2% y/y in May, following +2.1% y/y in March. The decline was mainly driven by Middle East disruption, with Middle Eastern carrier traffic down 46.6% and 28.4% y/y in April and May, respectively. While June passenger data are not yet published, flight tracking suggests Gulf carrier operations recovered to around 90% of normal levels by mid-June, implying a sequential improvement from a very depressed base. In early June, IATA cut its 2026 passenger traffic growth forecast to 2.1% from 4.9% previously, now substantially below the ~3% level Amadeus had previously indicated could still support the lower end of guidance. While pricing, mix, disruption-related revenues and cost actions provide important offsets, the further escalation in the region has reduced our confidence in the company's ability to deliver within the lower end of its guidance range. We therefore model FY26 revenue growth of 6.5% cc y/y, reflecting a more conservative recovery trajectory than implied by the current outlook. Based on this, we see an increased likelihood that management adopts a more cautious stance on FY26 expectations.

In Air Distribution, we expect bookings to remain under pressure. Q1 benefited from two strong months before a sharp March deterioration, whereas Q2 likely reflects weak activity throughout. While cancellations improved versus March, forward bookings remained subdued and May showed no meaningful rebound. We therefore expect bookings of 111.9m vs cons at 113.9m, down 6% y/y, with revenue per booking of E6.93, up 4.5% cc y/y, resulting in Air Distribution revenue of E773m (vs cons at E772m), down 1.4% cc y/y. In Air IT, we expect PB growth to slow materially versus Q1. PB growth weakened further in April and May showed only modest improvement. June is the key swing factor for whether PB growth is positive or negative for the quarter. We expect PB decline of 0.9% y/y, with revenue per PB of E1.08, up 7.3% cc y/y, resulting in Air IT revenue of E616.5m vs cons at E609.8m, up 6.3% cc y/y. Pricing should remain supportive, although the disruption-related uplift seen in Q1 should moderate. In HOS, we expect revenue of E276.1m vs cons at E276.2m, up 9.8% cc y/y. Growth should slow versus Q1 despite continued inorganic support. While less exposed than Air Distribution and Air IT, the segment is not immune, particularly in transactional areas such as hotel distribution, payments and media. M&A should provide some support, but not enough to offset weaker organic trends. On costs, we expect fixed-cost growth to remain well contained at ~3.6% y/y, supporting Q2 EBITDA of E644m vs cons at E654m and a margin of 38.7%.

Overall, we see Q2 as a trough for volumes, with Air Distribution bookings clearly negative and Air IT PB growth materially below Q1. Resilient unit revenues should cushion the impact, but the focus is on guidance. While some recovery has

ATOSS Software (Buy) – Q2 likely solid, but little to change the narrative ATOSS is due to report its Q2/26 results on 24 July. With the evolving agentic AI paradigm weighing on sentiment and limited near-term evidence of its long-term impact, shares remain stuck in the “disadvantaged by AI” bucket, alongside many other Application Software/SaaS names experiencing a narrative-driven de-rating. This is despite the overall solid Q1/26 print, with fundamentals continuing to contradict the “AI disruption” narrative, as NRR (112%) and GRR remained stable, while Cloud ARR growth of 27% was still robust. The only negative in the Q1/26 print that raised investor questions (based on our recent discussions) was the flat sequential increase in Cloud & Subscription order backlog in absolute terms, despite the completed GTM transformation and S&M hiring in FY25. The company attributed this to a weaker macro environment, though some investors remain cautious as to whether this could represent an early indication of AI-related headwinds, based on our discussions. We therefore expect the market to focus on these KPIs and leading indicators to assess any potential AI impact, with some nervousness likely should ATOSS disappoint here, even if primarily macro-driven.

That said, we anticipate a decent Q2, helped by comps looking more favorable following a weaker Q2 last year. We model revenues growing ~13% to ~E52m, implying a slight acceleration versus Q1 as sales hires from 2025 continue to ramp up, partly offset by a somewhat weaker macro and the industry-wide trend of budget reprioritization. Growth should be driven primarily by Software (Q2e +15%), particularly Cloud (Q2e +26%), supported by Q1 Cloud ARR of ~E110m and Cloud order backlog of ~E114m. We expect Q2 EBIT margins of ~35%, broadly flat sequentially (with Q1 benefiting from a smaller one-off) but remaining above ATOSS's updated FY26 guidance (≥34%).

All considered, we believe shares trading at ~17x FY27E uFCF look attractive for a company with ATOSS' growth profile, continuously expanding margins, and healthy cash conversion. We acknowledge multiples reflect long-term AI uncertainty, likely limiting near-term outperformance absent meaningful estimate revisions, with a decent Q2 likely providing little to shift the near-term AI narrative. That said, we see a significant portion of downside risk as already priced in, and view concerns around the pace of potential AI disruption as overstated, with the market potentially underappreciating the ability of incumbent software vendors to adapt. We maintain our Buy but lower our target price to E100 based on updated peer multiples.
AutoStore (Hold) – 2026 had a good start to the year...

During its Q1 results which built on the positive momentum of Q425, AutoStore talked about a positive start to 2026 with improving activity levels and increased confidence in long-term automation. In the current geopolitical landscape, this increasingly reflects a growing emphasis on resilient supply chains. While market volatility persists, momentum remained strong across several segments, including retail, 3PL, and industrial with increased demand for high throughput solutions. Growth in North America was particularly strong combined with a deeper level of customer engagement vs. in the past. This is particularly pleasing given the region was a focus of investment (with more direct support for customers) given the size of the opportunity.

Dassault Systemes (Hold) – Q2 likely broadly in line, but H2-weighted FY26 still carries execution risk

Dassault reports Q2/26 on 23 July, where we expect an in-line quarter, with revenue likely to land around the midpoint of guidance for 2-5% cc growth (DB ~4%). Based on our checks, while the macro backdrop remains fluid and there is still deal-timing sensitivity towards quarter-end, there has so far been no meaningful impact on deal conversions that would lead Dassault to miss on the quarter. That said, if current macro conditions persisted, we would not rule out some macro headwinds in the second half. We expect Medidata to remain in decline in Q2, while Centric growth should normalize from an exceptional Q1, stepping down sequentially but still supporting the expected mid-teens H1 trajectory. Mainstream Innovation should therefore maintain robust growth, underpinned by SolidWorks, while Industrial Innovation should remain stable at mid-single-digit growth, helped by normalizing comps rather than any material underlying softening in demand. While Medidata bookings continue to trend positively, supporting the better H2-vs-H1 thesis, we still expect negative growth in Life Sciences in Q2, with large contracts signed in prior quarters still ramping and not yet moving the needle in terms of revenue growth. On the backdrop of macro uncertainties, we expect Dassault to guide relatively cautiously for Q3 while confirming full-year guidance, putting greater weight on stronger Q4 seasonality and execution to reach at least the upper end of the full year guidance range. The bottom line is we expect Dassault to deliver against relatively modest expectations for Q2, but Q2 itself is unlikely to be a major catalyst for the stock, with investor focus remaining on H2 execution and the CMD in November. While the valuation has taken a substantial beating this year, we believe further proof points around the Medidata H2 acceleration (and sustained growth beyond) are needed to drive a sustained re-rating. Until then and with some macro risks looming we remain on the sidelines and lower our target price to E20, valuing Dassault on a 50/50 blend of FY26 P/E and EV/uFCF of ~15x and ~16x, respectively, at a discount to peers to reflect lower revenue and earnings growth. Hexagon (Hold) – Robotics remains a missed opportunity

Hexagon is set to publish its Q2/26 results on 29 July following completion of the Octave spin-off and recent CMD (see analysis here). For Q2/26, we forecast total revenue of E955m, with 6.1% organic growth in-line with cons at 6.1%. We expect Infrastructure & Geospatial (previously Geosystems) to post 2.0% y/y organic growth with weakness in China likely to persist which could be partially offset by strength in North American while the Middle East situation might continue to weigh on the EMEA region. We expect the Autonomous Solutions division to see 14.0% y/y organic growth as we see strong activity in the Aerospace & Defense sector to continue but with likely some growth moderation against tough comps into H2. For Manufacturing Intelligence, we expect 7.0% y/y organic growth in Q2/26 where we expect the order wins in FY25 to reflect in FY26 revenue while China Auto softness could become more of a headwind into H2, in our view. We do not yet model a contribution from the Robotics divisions in group financials as we await a strategic decision on the direction of this business and more progress on customer wins following an underwhelming update at the CMD that left too many outcomes open in a fast developing market where investors would have appreciated a clear "doubling down" on robotics. In our view, Hexagon should commit to becoming a leading European robotics OEM with investments on the continent and globally in capacity over being a component supplier or partner of other OEMs robots. We view the product (Aeon) as good enough to be successful in this market and believe a strategic commitment by management on robotics would be a strong positive for the share price. Hexagon has given a TAM estimate of $34b by 2035 based on an external report during the CMD. This includes majority TAM of $31b for industrial which we see as Aeon's main target market and a remaining $3b for Home which we believe can be substantially larger but also more competitive and less of a focus for Aeon.

Based on latest DB research (link here), we expect the potential installed base for industrial/manufacturing humanoid robots to be 7.6m units by 2050. The company has earlier announced a successful pilot with Schaeffler followed by agreement to deploy 1,000 Aeon robots. It would be interesting to note updates around other projects with BMW, Pilatus, and Fill as well as further pilots or commercial deals.

On profitability, we forecast EBITAC margin (ex robotics) of ~23% and EBIT margin of 26.5% which is ~270 bps lower y/y due to significant FX headwinds and weaker volumes. For FY26, we expect organic revenue growth of ~5.7% y/y with Autonomous Solutions growth somewhat normalizing against tougher comps. However, we expect significant FX headwinds to result in a y/y decline in reported revenue. In terms of profitability, we expect EBITAC margins to reach ~24.0% and EBIT margins of ~27% which is flat y/y as we expect FX headwinds to offset the benefits from the ongoing cost rationalization program. We keep our estimates mostly unchanged after we updated the model for the Octave spin-off. However, we update the model for FX changes resulting in a 1%/2% change in FY26/FY27 EPS. We also include the Waygate acquisition in our SOTP valuation.

With underlying growth likely moderating somewhat after a strong Q1 and robotics still a side show, we remain on the sidelines for now and rate Hexagon Hold. We value the company using a SOTP and apply a FY27e EV/EBIT multiple of ~18x to Hexagon and -18x for the Waygate acquisition which broadly in-line with European Industrial peers. Hexagon's stake in Cadence is valued at market prices but we understand that the company is reducing this stake currently in the market. Proforma FY27 net debt is adjusted for the Waygate acquisition.

Mensch und Maschine (Buy) – lower 3-year renewal cohort continues to weigh on growth

Mensch und Maschine is due to report Q2 results on 21 July, which we expect to be another quarter of muted growth. This is despite still favorable comps in Digitization, as Q2 last year was impacted by headwinds related to the Autodesk partner model transition. However, the Autodesk reselling business remains impacted by a smaller cohort of 3-year contract renewals, weighing on growth. On reseller margins, discussions with partners suggest some volatility due to Autodesk's revised partner incentives structure, which increasingly prioritizes new business and selected products over renewals. Given that new business represents a smaller share of MuM's Autodesk reselling, we believe the company is not yet able to fully offset this dynamic, which also represents a drag on growth. That said, we expect a slight sequential acceleration in Digitization, supported by a stronger services contribution. Growth in the Software segment should continue to outpace Digitization, albeit not sufficiently to reach the mid-point of the guidance range of 6–10%. We hence continue to expect FY26 gross profit growth to land below the mid-term target range, at ~5-6%. On profitability, we expect EBIT and EPS to continue to grow disproportionately strong in Q2 on the back of last year's cost-saving measures. However, we note that the exceptionally strong growth in Q1 was supported by a one-off gain related to the disposal of a stake in a SOFiSTiK subsidiary. We hence continue to see FY26 EBIT/EPS growth trending towards the lower end of the 11-19% mid-term ambition, broadly in line with recent management commentary.
Nemetschek (Buy) - Expecting a guidance update with Q2 to include HCSS

Nemetschek is due to report Q2 results on 30 July. Focus will be on the expected guidance update to include HCSS, as well as further commentary around the acquisition, including implications of Thoma Bravo's minority stake in the B&C segment. On guidance, we expect Nemetschek to maintain its current organic growth outlook of 14–15% cc, with HCSS adding a high-single-digit percentage contribution to FY26 growth (DBe ~9%, although we note some uncertainty around the size of potential revenue haircuts at HCSS). We also expect an update to EBITDA guidance (32-33% pre-HCSS), where we now see Nemetschek coming in at the lower end (DBe ~32%) or potentially even below, due to one-off costs related to the acquisition.

Ocado (Buy) – Expected to be on track, investor focus also on recently announced leadership transition
DB forecasts in line with guidance

As a reminder, for FY26, the group is guiding for c. £500m of Tech Solutions revenue and c. 30% adj. EBITDA margin. Logistics is expected to deliver c. £30-35m of adj. EBITDA on the back of mid-to high-single-digit revenue growth. Note the Tech Solutions guidance reflects c. 10 new modules expected in FY26, offsetting the 12 modules from the Kroger and Sobeys closures in early 2026. The group then expects a further 10-15 modules in FY27. Overall, 6 CFCs are expected to go live over the next 2-3 years. Focus on the cost base remains strong with total cash costs across Technology and Support in FY27 to reduce by around £150m relative to FY25. The group has reiterated that it expects to turn cash flow positive during H2'26 - but that for underlying cash outflow to still be c.£(200)m for the year as a whole. It expects to be full-year cash flow positive in FY27. Our forecasts are essentially in line with these forecasts. Note that FY26 revenue and adj. EBITDA figures will be impacted by the accounting treatment of the Kroger Letter of Credit and Kroger and Sobeys CFC closure fees. The impact on FY26 revenue and adj. EBITDA is c £350m. Whilst not treated as exceptional items, we highlight our revenue, adj. EBITDA and adj. FD EPS figures including and excluding these items given its distorting impact.

As such, for H1, pre these accounting Letter of Credit and closure fees, we are looking for revenue of £658m and adj. EBITDA of £77.8m. Including these items, we are looking for revenue of £973m and adj. EBITDA of £393m. Note that the recently announced Asda partnership is not expected to have any material impact in FY26. With Asda having over £3bn of online sales and assuming an Ocado take rate of c. 1% for these technologies, we assumed an annualised revenue contribution of c. £25-30m. We would expect this to have a very high drop through to EBITDA (around 70-80%). We assumed a partial contribution in FY27 (c. £7m to adj. EBITDA) and a full run-rate in FY28 (c.£20m to adj. EBITDA).

Ocado also recently provided further clarity on the next phase of its long-term leadership transition. The Board and CEO Tim Steiner have been engaged in a succession planning process designed to support Ocado's long-term success. The process is expected to conclude around the start of the 2028 financial year. ATOSS is a leader in the German-speaking workforce management (WFM) market, offering software for optimized personnel deployment, focusing on industries such as manufacturing, retail and healthcare. The company's advanced solutions help ensure that clients have the right number of employees, with the right skills available, at the right place, time and cost. ATOSS is a high-quality business, with visibility for consistent growth in the mid-teens, industry-leading profitability and healthy cash conversion, driven by the (largely) completed GTM transformation, accelerating European expansion, and an anticipated pick-up in cloud migration.

We value ATOSS based on a 50/50 blend of a peer-based valuation and DCF, to reflect ATOSS's relatively predictable growth and stable cash flows over the long term. For relative valuation, we value ATOSS at a slight premium to the average FY26E EV/uFCF multiple of ATOSS' peer group (in line with the average historical premium). Stronger performance, clean financials and a healthy balance sheet together with higher cash returns and an overall better growth outlook over the long term should warrant a premium, in our view. For our DCF, we assume a WACC of ~9.4%, derived from a risk-free rate of ~2.5%, a risk premium of 6% and beta of ~1.2 (broadly in line with BBG historical beta). We also assume a cash tax rate of 32% and a terminal growth rate of ~2%.

Downside risks to our view include: 1) slower-than-expected European expansion; 2) a worsening macro environment impacting software spend (especially in DACH); 3) issues associated with the cloud migration (e.g., higher churn, slower progress, etc.); 4) potentially value-destructive M&A; 5) the prospect of further placing by major shareholders creating an overhang on the share price; 6) growing exposure to SMEs (higher churn, higher sensitivity to economic development, etc.); 7) adverse changes in regulation (labor laws, etc.); 8) failure to launch new products/technology; and 9) increased competition.

AutoStore operates in the warehouse automation space which has a lot of structural drivers given businesses need to drive efficiency, save costs, improve accuracy and meeting increasing demands from customers. AutoStore has pioneered and is the market leader in robotic, cube-based AS/RS (automated storage and retrieval system), which has seen strong adoption due to its flexibility, performance and ROI. Performance in the last 12-18 months has been impacted by a weaker macro economic backdrop, exacerbated by tariff-related uncertainties earlier in the year. As such, revenues and earnings have been volatile in Q1/Q2 but this has gradually recovered in Q3 and was much improved in Q4. Medium-term, the group has a proven record of landing and expanding with customers and with 70-80% of warehouses globally still relying heavily on manual processes, there is a strong medium-term growth opportunity.

Our target price is based on an 18x EV/EBITDA 1-yr forward multiple, broadly in line with the wider industrial automation peers. This is supported by a reverse DCF using a 9% WACC, LT EBIT margins of 38%, medium-term growth rate of 12% and terminal growth of 3%. There has been considerable volatility in the group's performance so extrapolating to longer term trends has its risks.

Risks include: 1) end customers propensity to buy multi-million dollar systems will be impacted by macroeconomic conditions; 2) systems are predominantly a capex purchase and can result in a lumpy revenue profile; 3) some deals are now moving more to an as-a-service model - where revenue recognition is over a much longer period of time potentially creating revenue gaps near term; 4) there are competing warehouse automation technologies and there is no guarantee the group's type of system will continue to win share; 5) the group works with distribution partners to get their product to market - loss of a key partner could impact revenue materially; 6) the impact of President Trump's tariffs on the group (aluminum is the key material in the group's system) is still hard to measure - NA sales is c.25% of total); 7) any disruption in its supply chain/ production facilities (Poland and Thailand) could impact customers and revenues; 8) there is also currency risk with most revenues in EUR and USD and most costs in NOK, PLN and EUR. On the upside, the main risk is an improvement in the macro backdrop that is better and faster than we anticipate in our forecasts. There is also a possible improvement in its win-rate either through better sales execution, a more appealing model or a combination of both.

Bechtle projects a positive trajectory but also continuously highlights challenges such as rising manufacturer prices and potential supply constraints. The company indicated that it feels well positioned in this challenging environment, given its size and reliability as a preferred partner for its larger suppliers. Bechtle is also expected to significantly benefit from the German stimulus package later this year. Bechtle entered 2026 with good momentum and a record order backlog, contributing to an optimistic sentiment. Management has also confirmed that many SMEs have indeed postponed their orders for too long and now need to order, irrespective of pricing levels. Public sector activity has resumed after FY25 which was negatively affected by various headwinds in that customer segment. Robust public sector demand in Germany offers a solid base, but the impact of higher memory chip prices on sales and product mix creates uncertainty for EBT margin expansion. Bechtle guides for business volume to rise 5-10% yoy (DBe +8% yoy), while revenue (DBe +5% yoy) and EBT (DBe +5% yoy) are envisaged to increase 0-5% yoy. Bechtle expects profitability "to be influenced by investments in our internal IT and our M&A activities" and, according to our estimates, these investments could result in an approximate 3% absolute EBT or 15bps EBT margin headwind, implying that the "only stable" margin guidance is not solely a function of the still challenging business environment. Unfortunately, Bechtle remains unwilling to quantify the exact internal IT investment or its timing. Hence, our best estimate remains the "high-single-digit million-euro amount" mentioned at the FY25 analyst meeting, to be spent equally over the quarters of FY26. Despite the prevailing lack of transparency, management appears optimistic about achieving a reliable view on FY26 by mid-2026. Given the reduced visibility, the company's guidance will be reviewed more frequently this year. Discussions with major suppliers regarding the FY26 back-end margin appear to be finalized, with CFO Jehle indicating that more contracts are now based on value rather than volume thresholds, which is beneficial for Bechtle. Bechtle should significantly benefit from the German stimulus package. While we deem it highly likely that this will materialize, not least because public sector business accounts for approximately 40% of group revenue, we believe it will take until at least the end of FY26 for Bechtle to fully benefit. Bechtle targets a FY30 EBT margin of 5% (compared to 3.8% in FY25 based on business volume) and a business volume exceeding EUR 10bn (from EUR 8.6bn in FY25, implying a 3% CAGR). This leads to an implied EBT CAGR of 9%. Current investments, while weighing on the EBT margin, should ultimately contribute to achieving this target.

We equally weight two valuation approaches. Our fundamental valuation, derived from a standard three-stage DCF model, uses a WACC of 6.7%, based on a risk-free interest rate of 3.0%, a risk premium of 6%, a beta of 1.16, and a 55% equity ratio. This yields a valuation of EUR 45.05. Our relative, multiples-based valuation is the average of Bechtle's 10-year P/E, EV/EBIT, EV/EBITDA, and EV/Sales applied to our FY27E estimates, yielding a per-share value of EUR 45.72. Equally weighted, our target price is EUR 45, rounded from EUR 45.38. We maintain our Buy rating.

Despite the challenging IT market, CANCOM identifies opportunities by leveraging prevailing conditions such as supply bottlenecks, rising DRAM prices due to the shift towards AI-related memory technologies and increasing component costs across the industry. The company believes it is well-positioned to capitalize on these trends through its extensive network of 300 manufacturer partners, which enables it to effectively manage supply chain complexities. Additionally, CANCOM's broad and diversified customer base of over 40,000 clients limits its dependency on individual, large business partners. Management also anticipates benefiting from the ongoing AI boom (e.g., AWS, Anthropic), as CANCOM's customers require reliable partners to implement these new technologies. We continue to expect customer demand for infrastructure solutions, digitalization, AI transformation, and data sovereignty to positively influence the 2026 financial year, with demand foremost coming from the public sector. However, this will most likely be juxtaposed with anticipated significant price increases and uncertainties surrounding the availability of IT components. CANCOM should significantly benefit from the German stimulus package, although we admit that it should take until the end of FY26 at the earliest to see the company benefiting. CANCOM is also participating in several larger tenders with the public sector, so momentum is picking up further. But the company does not only see the public sector coming back again but also that the SMEs start with upgrades of both soft- as well as hardware.

We use two equally-weighted valuation approaches: our standard three-stage DCF model and an IT service peer group comparison. This leads to an estimated value of EUR 36.97 per share. We reiterate our Buy rating and keep our price target of EUR 34. Based on our FY27E forecasts, CANCOM currently trades at a 66% discount to its peer group's EV/EBITDA multiple. While this discount is largely attributable to several negative surprises in recent quarters, we hope to see it diminish over the next couple of months, as we expect CANCOM's performance to underscore the achievability of the FY26 guidance.

CANCOM derives the bulk of its revenue from Germany. Given that the IT market is largely correlated with general economic conditions, a macro slowdown could lead to cuts in IT spending. Another major downside risk is the potential entrance of a large IT vendor into the SME market.

Mensch und Maschine (MuM) is a leading European Autodesk partner providing software and digitization services for the architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) and manufacturing industries. A change in the accounting treatment of its Autodesk business as a result of the shift in Autodesk's go-to-market motion temporarily distorts MuM's FY25 financials, we believe masking the underlying strength of the company. We see this transition year as an attractive entry point, with MuM trading at a significant discount to its 10-year EV/EBIT multiple. We believe shares can re-rate to historical valuation levels once MuM resumes its normal trajectory of robust EPS growth in '26/'27, driven by reaccelerating growth and margin expansion. Buy.

MuM combines a Software segment that can be compared to engineering software companies, while the reseller business exhibits characteristics of IT services and consulting. We, hence, use a SOTP approach when valuing MuM, as we believe the VAR business should be valued differently from its faster-growing, higher-margin Software business. We value the Software segment at ~17x EV/EBIT, at a 25% discount to the median of comparable engineering software companies. This discount reflects a slightly less dominant market position and the smaller TAM of MuM's software brands, as well as a discount, given our estimates being slightly below consensus. The Digitization segment is valued at ~12x EV/EBIT, the median of a broad group of IT services and VAR peers. We adjust for minorities (fully consolidated in the Software segment), valued at ~19x P/E, a 25% discount to the median P/E of our engineering software peer group. Combined, we derive our target price, which assumes a 21x FY26 P/E versus MuM's key peer trading on 25x when adj. for SBC. Hence, although our estimates for outer years are below consensus, we view valuation levels as compelling. Buy.

Key downside risks to our view include, but are not limited to: 1) MuM's dependence on Autodesk, 2) risks associated with changes in Autodesk's pricing model, 3) intensified competition and consolidation trends in the Autodesk partner channel, 4) MuM's exposure to cyclical end markets, 5) risks associated with innovation and technological advancements, 6) potentially value-destructive M&A activity in the future, and 7) risks associated with MuM's shareholder structure.

Temenos is a leader in the core banking software market, a large market that industry analysts expect to grow at an ~8% CAGR over the medium term, driven by digitization, regulation, and a switch from in-house to third-party software as banks look to reduce total cost of ownership. We believe that Temenos is differentiated from its competitors by its sustained high level of product development investment and strong ecosystem partnerships. However, we believe the Covid-19 pandemic resulted in a more challenging end-market environment among banks for some time and that core banking initiatives may drop down the IT agenda as a result. We rate the stock a Hold.

We value Temenos on a simple average of 19x '27e P/E and 18x '27 EV/uFCF. Our multiples are at a slight premium to peers reflecting company's recurring revenue mix, improved execution while still allowing for usual delivery risks inherent in a multi-year transition story.

Key upside risks include: 1) a less-severe downturn in the banking industry than we expect, 2) a mega-deal signing boosting license revenue, 3) more traction in expansion markets than we expect, and 4) subscription and SaaS revenue ramping up faster than anticipated. Key downside risks include: 1) a more severe downturn in the banking industry than we expect, 2) execution misses on implementation, 3) share loss to competition, and 4) execution misses on SaaS and subscription that leads to medium-term targets being revisited.

Macroeconomic fluctuations often account for most of the risks associated with exposures to instruments that promise to pay fixed or variable interest rates. For an investor who is long fixed-rate instruments (thus receiving these cash flows), increases in interest rates naturally lift the discount factors applied to the expected cash flows and thus cause a loss. The longer the maturity of a certain cash flow and the higher the move in the discount factor, the higher will be the loss. Upside surprises in inflation, fiscal funding needs, and FX depreciation rates are among the most common adverse macroeconomic shocks to receivers. But counterparty exposure, issuer creditworthiness, client segmentation, regulation (including changes in assets holding limits for different types of investors), changes in tax policies, currency convertibility (which may constrain currency conversion, repatriation of profits and/or liquidation of positions), and settlement issues related to local clearing houses are also important risk factors. The sensitivity of fixed-income instruments to macroeconomic shocks may be mitigated by indexing the contracted cash flows to inflation, to FX depreciation, or to specified interest rates - these are common in emerging markets. The index fixings may - by construction - lag or mis-measure the actual move in the underlying variables they are intended to track. The choice of the proper fixing (or metric) is particularly important in swaps markets, where floating coupon rates (i.e., coupons indexed to a typically short-dated interest rate reference index) are exchanged for fixed coupons. Funding in a currency that differs from the currency in which coupons are denominated carries FX risk. Options on swaps (swaptions) the risks typical to options in addition to the risks related to rates movements.
